solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Catamaran ordered to transport grand historic document

indicators.note: to transport something is to carry it, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
the letters of the boat are put in a new order, signalling an anagram

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A twin-hulled boat is used to ferry an important old charter somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges CATAMARAN into MANACARTA, and 'to transport' has those letters carry G.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1215 charter sealed by King John is the most famous historic document in English constitutional history.

clue.text: I miss pub: sort that's put out special ribbons?

indicators.note: things put out of place are disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone laments missing the pub, a kind of person who is easily annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges the letters of I MISS PUB SORT. The question mark admits the definition is playful: a one-sided twisted band is hardly an ordinary ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: These are loops of paper given a half twist before joining, so they are ribbons with a single surface and edge.

clue.text: Actress filling sugar bowls and cigar boxes

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words like filling inside a container

explanation.surface: An actress is stuffing sugar bowls and cigar boxes with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' signals letters inside a run of words; the name sits in suGAR BOwls, and again in ciGAR BOxes, a double helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Girl's warning oddly ignored

definitions.note: the clue reads 'girl is', so the definition is just a girl's name

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A girl's warning is being strangely disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of WARNING leaves the 2nd, 4th and 6th. 'Girl's' stands for 'girl is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common female first name, so it fits a clue asking for any girl.

clue.text: An uncannily grim, upsetting story, that's initially impressive

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: A disturbing ghost story is described as making a strong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of An Uncannily Grim Upsetting Story That's.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means inspiring awe and reverence, a synonym of imposing or impressive.

clue.text: Male deity unexpectedly requiring a pause in operation?

indicators.note: the letters turn up in a surprising order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A god appears out of nowhere and demands that work stop for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate interval before a mechanism acts, such as a fuse or a bank vault lock, is a pause in operation.

clue.text: Keep signalling vessel

parts.note: to flag is to signal, as with a flag waved at a passing car
on means continuing, as in keep on or carry on

explanation.surface: An order to carry on signalling to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'keep flagging' becomes FLAG plus ON, with ON standing for continuing.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bottle or jug for wine or ale is a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Luther's prose adapted for stuffy artisans?

indicators.note: the writing is reworked into a new form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Martin Luther's writing is being revised for some dull, pompous craftsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges LUTHERS PROSE. 'Stuffy' seems to mean dull but really means stuffing furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftspeople who pad and cover sofas and chairs fill them with stuffing, so they are jokingly stuffy workers.

clue.text: Farm building containing old cut of beef

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing hay or housing animals

explanation.surface: A barn on a farm with an old joint of beef hanging inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef is a large joint made of both sirloins left joined at the backbone.

clue.text: Girl's tunic boy picked up by mistake

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the name is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: Jim is a boy's name
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: A boy has grabbed a girl's school tunic in error.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pinafore dress was the traditional uniform for British schoolgirls, worn for sport and lessons.

clue.text: A French work put forward without being challenged

parts.note: un is the French for a
OP is short for opus, a musical work
posed means put forward, as of a question

explanation.surface: A French piece of work is submitted and nobody objects to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate or motion facing no opposition goes through with nobody contesting it.

clue.text: Metal rod, old penny and diamonds for gambling game

parts.note: a poker is the metal rod for stirring a fire
D stood for the old British penny, from Latin denarius
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A list of items, a rod, a coin and gems, staked on a game of chance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a game of chance played with dice marked with card values instead of spots.

clue.text: Syrupy stuff, mostly wholesome

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: good means wholesome, as in good food

explanation.surface: A sweet sticky substance that is largely healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Any sticky, viscous substance, syrup included, is informally called by this word.

clue.text: Small pieces of coal, loose

definitions.meaning: coal dust and small fragments left after screening are sold under this name
not taut, as a rope that hangs limply

explanation.surface: Fragments of coal are lying about loose.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both coal dust left after screening and rope that is not pulled tight.

clue.text: "England": book penned by a famous author

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the outer pieces hold the next one

parts.note: a literary lion is a celebrated author

explanation.surface: A book called England was written by a celebrated writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing but means enclosed: A plus LION shut around B.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ancient, poetic name for Britain, often used for England in particular.

clue.text: The two letters often associated with Lowry's estate

parts.words: The two letters often associated with Lowry's
parts.note: the painter Lowry is always known by his initials L. S., read here with the word between them

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the initials linked with a painter's property.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of industrial northern scenes; spell out his two initials with the joining word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a piece of property consisting of tracts of ground, so the plural noun for grounds fits.

clue.text: Nude DA, wandering around like a zombie?

indicators.note: the letters roam about out of place, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A naked district attorney is shambling about like a corpse risen from the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A zombie is a reanimated corpse, among creatures neither fully alive nor properly dead.

clue.text: Rag and bone

definitions.meaning: to rag is to tease or make fun of someone
one of the curved bones around the chest

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to tease someone playfully and one of the curved bones of the chest.

clue.text: Remedy nun concocted in historic English meadow

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A nun brews a herbal cure in a field steeped in history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames-side meadow in Surrey is where the Magna Carta was sealed in 1215.

clue.text: Dodge publicity, going in the night before

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: an eve is the evening before an event, like Christmas Eve
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Someone avoids the press by slipping in the evening before.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or escape it by cunning.

clue.text: Kit out for short film recording

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the recording is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a video is a recording on film or tape

explanation.surface: Equipment being acquired for making a short film.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit someone out is to equip or supply them with what they need.

clue.text: One hundred and fifty live in part of Ireland

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
to live is to exist, as in they are

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people reside in an Irish district.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county on the west coast of Ireland, in the province of Munster.

clue.text: Vehicle that's about right

parts.note: ca. abbreviates circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A motor described as being roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle for carrying a few passengers on roads.

clue.text: Look after sea eagles, small, being kind

parts.note: to tend is to care for
erns or ernes are sea eagles, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A caring person looks after little sea eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kind, as a noun phrase, describes gentle affectionate care, a synonym of fondness.
